historical_references.reference: Tehvansh was the name of a powerful Yadava king who ruled over the region of Mathura during the Mahabharata era.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic attributed to Vyasa, consisting of over 100,000 verses in Sanskrit. It is considered one of the two major Sanskrit epics, the other being the Ramayana. The Mahabharata is a narrative of the Kurukshetra war, a familial conflict between two branches of a kuru clan.

historical_references.reference: Tehvansh, also known as Vajranabh, was the great-grandson of Krishna and the founder of the Vatsa dynasty in Magadha, now modern-day Bihar. He ruled around the 5th century BCE.
historical_references.context: The Vatsa dynasty was a branch of the Haihayas, who traced their descent from the lunar god, the moon. Vajranabh is believed to have established the Vajjian confederacy in eastern India, which was one of the leading powers in the region during the late Vedic and early Mahajanpada periods.
